author: 13WHAM
title: Sodus double murder accomplice admits lying under oath at 2019 trial amid resentencing bid
text:
A woman convicted in connection with a 2018 double homicide in Sodus admitted Thursday that she previously lied under oath as prosecutors challenged her credibility during the second day of her resentencing hearing.
Wayne County District Attorney Christine Callanan questions Charlene Childers during the second day of her resentencing hearing in Wayne County Court in Lyons, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026.
Lyons, N.Y. — A woman convicted in connection with a 2018 double homicide in Sodus admitted Thursday that she previously lied under oath as prosecutors challenged her credibility during the second day of her resentencing hearing. Charlene Childers, 33, is seeking a reduced sentence under New York's Domestic Violence Survivors Justice Act.
She is serving a 28-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to manslaughter and a weapons charge in connection with the killings of her ex-boyfriend, Joshua Niles, and his fiancée, Amber Washburn, outside their home on Carlton Street in Sodus. Wayne County District Attorney Christine Callanan cross-examined Childers for much of Thursday, questioning inconsistencies between her current testimony, previous statements and evidence in the case.
Childers testified about alleged abuse during her relationship with Niles and years of custody disputes involving their children. She also acknowledged that the custody dispute was the reason she wanted Niles killed. Callanan challenged Childers' account, pointing to statements she said did not match the evidence. The district attorney also referenced police reports involving Childers and Niles, some of which documented allegations of physical abuse but noted no physical evidence of a fight.
During questioning, Childers admitted lying under oath when she previously testified against her then-husband, Timothy Dean, at his 2019 murder trial. Her testimony was part of a negotiated plea agreement that allowed her to receive a sentence shorter than life in prison. Childers also acknowledged meeting with her attorneys to prepare for the resentencing hearing, including reviewing the legal requirements and questions she expected to face.
"The entire examination that I conducted today was trying to demonstrate to the court and build a record that she's aware of the proceedings that she's participating in," Callanan said. "She's aware of the requirements that she would have to meet to get the benefit of the reduced sentence, and ultimately make the argument to the court that she is biased, that she has a reason not to tell the truth, and that she's doing all of this to receive a benefit.
And her credibility is at issue before this court. So the judge needs to be able to understand all of that.
" Prosecutors said Childers helped orchestrate the 2018 killings with Dean, who was convicted of murder and is serving a life sentence. The three-day hearing is expected to continue Friday, when a psychologist serving as an expert witness for the defense is scheduled to testify. The judge is not required to issue a decision at the conclusion of the hearing, and there is no deadline for a ruling on Childers' resentencing request.
